Subject: Unit economics deep-dive: pricing & token volumes

Hi Alex — great conversation earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we're aligned: 

Recap
- FintechX is planning a new conversational feature for onboarding and support (multi-turn chat + structured outputs).
- Pilot expected to cover ~1M active users/month initially with an estimated 2-4 prompts per user and average prompt size ~150 tokens (input+response). That implies ~450M-900M tokens/month depending on hit rates and caching.
- Target customer LTV and margin targets mean you need inference costs to be below ~$X per 1M tokens to hit feature-level margins (we discussed target $/1M tokens in the call).

Open items I promised to follow up on:
1) Example unit economics: translate inference $/1M tokens to $/feature and to gross margin impact given your pricing and CAC assumptions.
2) Provide a pricing estimate for the expected volume with tiered discounts for committed capacity (Dedicated vs hosted).
3) Attach a starter unit-econ workbook (attached) and a Redwood pricing estimate PDF.

Suggested next steps
- You: confirm expected daily MAU range (low/likely/high) and any seasonal spikes.
- Us: run a simple model mapping $/1M tokens to $/feature and CAC payback scenarios; include a Dedicated vs Hosted recommendation.
- Schedule a follow-up 30-45 minute session next week to walk the workbook and agree on a pilot commit if numbers look good.

I attached a short workbook (FintechX_unit_econ_v1.xlsx) with three scenarios and a Redwood pricing estimate. I cc'd Aditya (solutions) and Elliot (AE manager) to help scope the pilot and align on discounts.

Thanks — talk soon.

Marissa Cole

marissa@redwood.com | (415) 555-0142

Thanks Marissa — useful recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) MAU & usage profile: Low: 700k MAU, Likely: 1.1M MAU, High: 1.8M MAU. Average prompts per user: 3. Peak concurrency around US morning hours.
2) Prompt size: onboarding flows are heavier (avg ~250 tokens), support flows are lighter (avg ~90 tokens). Overall blended avg ~150 tokens is fine for planning.
3) Budget range: we have an initial Q2 pilot budget of $35k-$60k for infra + vendor fees. For a production rollout in H2 we can expand but need to see pilot economics.
4) Margin target: product leadership wants inference <= 20% of gross margin impact for the added feature. We can share target $/feature if you produce the mapping back to $/1M tokens.

I attached the usage export you asked for (excerpt) and Priya (ops) will pull more detailed logs if needed. Let us know where the breakout is most sensitive (input vs response tokens, cache hit assumptions, and quantization/throughput choices).

Alex — thanks, this is perfect and helps tighten the scenarios. Quick notes from our modeling and questions before we run a detailed workbook: 

Top-level: mapping approach
- We map tokens -> $/1M tokens (inference) -> $/feature by multiplying tokens/feature * $/1M tokens.
- Important levers: cache hit rate on reused prompts (saves output tokens), quantization & model family (affects $/1M tokens), and commitment level (hosted vs Dedicated pricing).

Preliminary numbers (high-level, ballpark) based on your blended 150 tokens/prompt and 3 prompts/user:
- Low (700k MAU): ~315M tokens/month -> hosted est $/1M tokens = $X_hosted -> monthly cost = $Y_hosted -> cost/feature = $Y_hosted / 2.1M features (700k*3).
- Likely (1.1M MAU): ~495M tokens/month -> hosted est $X_hosted -> monthly cost -> cost/feature.
- High (1.8M MAU): ~810M tokens/month -> Dedicated commitment likely becomes cost-effective; est $X_dedicated per 1M tokens -> monthly cost -> cost/feature.

Assumptions I used in the workbook (editable):
- Cache hit-rate: 15% (pilot)
- Prompt/response token split: 40/60
- Model: open-llm-v2 (quantized) equivalent performance; we'll swap to a higher-capacity model if you need better quality — that increases $/1M tokens ~20-45%.
- Infrastructure discounts: 10-25% on Dedicated depending on commit term.

Next asks before we lock numbers:
1) Confirm cache hit-rate expectations for onboarding flows (do you expect re-used system messages/templates?).
2) Confirm whether regulatory requirements force Private deployment (affects pricing).

Proposed follow-up: Elliot and I can run a 45-minute deep-dive Wed/Thu to walk the workbook line-by-line and show Dedicated vs Hosted cost curves. From there we can produce a pilot statement of work and commitment options that map back to your $35k-$60k pilot budget.

I'll attach an updated workbook after your answers and include a simple CAC payback sheet (unit economic: $/feature, expected conversion lift, CAC payback months) so product leadership can evaluate.

—
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
